lead_headline: AI SDK clears a backlog of Zod, file-handling, and telemetry fixes in a single afternoon
lead_body: Thirty-three commits landed in AI SDK today, patching Zod 4.4 compatibility, tool-result file downloads, and non-image file mapping in the OpenAI Responses provider. The sandbox API was quietly demoted to experimental, and the telemetry onFinish hook was renamed to onEnd — both worth checking before upgrading. Astro shipped five coordinated releases and opened Cloudflare fetch and Hono handlers as first-class export targets.
lead_article:
The busiest signal today belongs to AI SDK, which pushed through a sustained afternoon of fixes and documentation: Zod 4.4 compatibility restored in validateUIMessages, tool-result file URL downloads patched, non-image file parts correctly mapped in the OpenAI Responses provider, and a new performance statistics feature added. The rename of telemetry's onFinish to onEnd slipped in quietly between version bumps, and the sandbox API was demoted to experimental — both the kind of detail worth knowing before upgrading. Astro shipped a coordinated release across five packages (astro 6.3.2 among them), plus a PR opening Cloudflare fetch and Hono handlers as first-class export targets for advanced routing; the VSCode extension fix that preceded the release required reverting npm ci back to npm i, which suggests a toolchain wrinkle still being tidied.

Workflow SDK had a purposeful morning: three PRs arrived covering World.createRunId(), region-aware queue routing, a tagged ULID encode/decode sub-export, and a schema fix making run.input and step.input optional — the last of these probably prompted by the bug report that landed hours earlier about Zod rejecting RemoteRef-wrapped step inputs in production. Claude Code released v2.1.141 with changelog only, but the issue queue was loud: garbled display in agent view, mouse-tracking escape sequences leaking into prompts, background subagent zombie states triggering stop-hook loops, and AskUserQuestion cards silently dismissed on quit. Gemma.cpp opened a PR to remove Q transposition from the tiled attention kernel — a low-volume but architecturally meaningful change. Metaflow's single PR cleans up bare except clauses, which is unglamorous and correct.
